Hi David — thanks for the clear summary and the capacity estimates. Below is a compact qualification checklist plus our recommended milestones so you can present to procurement and engineering. I kept the language non-technical for PMs, with separate technical notes from Ben below.

Quick summary of tradeoffs (short):
- Hosted API (fastest onboarding): shared infra, best for early validation. We cannot provide single-tenant GPU guarantees here; we provide per-request QoS, dynamic throttles, and regional routing. Good if you can tolerate infrequent tail variance and want fastest time-to-value.
- Dedicated capacity (recommended for latency SLOs): reserved GPU pools assigned to your account. Isolation model: dedicated instance pools (no co-tenant scheduling on the same GPU), network segmentation, and optional KV-cache partitioning. This reduces noisy-neighbor risk and lets us meet tight p95 targets with pre-warming.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer-controlled network & optionally air-gapped. Longest lead time but maximum control (you own instance sizing, KMS, and data plane).

Noisy-neighbor mitigations we use (summary):
- Dedicated: physical pool assignments + scheduler-level reservation to avoid GPU oversubscription; per-tenant VM cgroup limits; pre-warmed models and reserved KV cache shards.
- Shared: dynamic backpressure, adaptive batching windows per customer token pattern, and burst isolation via per-API-key queues.

SLOs we can operationalize (examples — to be codified in an SLA):
- Latency: p50/p95 generation latency targets for 1–512 token responses; example: p95 < 120ms for 1–128 tokens (hosted may hit 200–300ms p95 during global spikes). Dedicated: p95 < 120ms for up to 512 tokens typically achievable with reserved pools.
- Availability: Hosted baseline 99.5%, Dedicated SLA options 99.9%+ with reserved capacity and fallbacks.
- Throughput: guaranteed concurrent request slots mapped to a committed QPS for Dedicated.

Qualification checklist (please confirm values):
- Peak concurrent RPS (API calls per second):
- Typical response token length and max expected token length:
- Required p95 latency target for your user experience (ms):
- Data residency / region requirement (us/eu/apac):
- Compliance docs required (SOC 2 / HIPAA / ISO):
- Procurement timeline target and primary contact (name/email):

Proposed decision milestones:
1) By Apr 20 — MedTidal returns checklist answers + procurement contact (you).
2) Apr 21–22 — Redwood provides short written recommendation (1 page) with cost banding for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and a preliminary SOW outline.
3) Week of Apr 26 — Technical POC planning call (we'll include Ben and an infra engineer) and security docs exchange (SOC 2 summary attached).
4) Target pilot start: May 3 (if Dedicated chosen, we'll reserve capacity; for Private, timeline adjusted).

Attachments and links:
- SOC 2 summary (linked): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/medtidal/rdw-soc2-summary.pdf
- Internal capacity/cost reference (for Ben to attach)

Next steps: please fill the checklist items above and I'll turn the answers into the 1-page recommendation and a simple SOW draft for procurement. If you prefer a quick 30-minute follow-up instead of written answers, I can propose slots next Tue/Wed.

Thanks — Irene
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up + noisy-neighbor / SLO concerns from today (technical notes)

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra perspective:
- If MedTidal requires p95 < 120ms at 512 tokens consistently, plan for Dedicated with pre-warmed pools (NVIDIA A100 / H100 class) and reserved KV cache partitions. Shared Hosted could meet the target for short bursts but risks tail variance under global load.
- We do per-customer GPU reservations (no co-scheduled third-party workloads on the same GPU) for Dedicated — this is how we remove noisy neighbor risk at the compute level.
- Network isolation: Dedicated includes VPC-level routing with private IPs; Private on-prem offers full control for egress filtering and KMS.
- Ops: For Dedicated we'll need a committed QPS and a lead time of ~10 business days to reserve and pre-warm capacity. For Private, estimate 4–6 weeks for on-prem or customer VPC deployment including security onboarding.

I'll attach a one-page capacity guide and a quick table mapping latency to instance class.
Attachments: rdw_capacity_guide_onepager.pdf

Happy to walk through the numbers on the POC planning call.

- Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
